grammar.title: The Verb 'Gustar' (To Like)
grammar.explanation:
In Spanish, 'gustar' works differently from English. Instead of 'I like something,' the structure is literally 'Something is pleasing to me':

• Me gusta + singular noun: Me gusta el pan. (I like bread.)
• Me gustan + plural noun: Me gustan las frutas. (I like fruits.)

The indirect object pronouns are: me (I), te (you), le (he/she/you formal), nos (we), les (they/you all).

To express dislike, add 'no' before the pronoun: No me gusta la carne. (I don't like meat.)
